name: Effluent release; from flat glass industry wastewater treatment plant
description: This unit process reflects effluent release for U.S. flat glass production facilities. The functional unit reflects treatment of 1 cubic meter of wastewater from a relevant facility. The scope of this process is limited to effluent release. Use the corresponding wastewater treatment process to reflect the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Current (2025) U.S. regulation for the flat glass industry, float glass production.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Effluent release to surface water from U.S. flat glass facilities - float glass production method. Effluent quality reflects use of chemically enhanced clarification, multi-media filtration (optional), and disinfection (optional) and dechlorination treatment processes.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: This process was developed to represent effluent release from onsite wastewater treatment at a generic U.S. flat glass production facility where the main pollutants of concern are total suspended solids, phosphorus and oil. Pollutants in the flat glass industry are regulated on the basis of unit mass per metric ton of product. The allowable pollutant concentrations could therefore vary widely depending on the quantity of wastewater produced, regarding which very limited data is available. A review of regulated facilities found that most have TSS limits of between 12 and 30 mg/L (monthly average) with a daily maximum of 24-45 mg/L. A review of DMR data for select facilities found that 0 mg TSS/liter is achievable with the specified treatment technology for this industry. A conservative estimate of 5 mg TSS/liter was used in this process. Other effluent concentrations were based on reported DMR data for the Guardian Industries, Carleton Plant (Michigan).
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Unregulated pollutants are excluded from the effluent inventory. This exclusion is not expected to significantly influence results. The effluent guidelines development document (see sources) indicates that BOD, COD, detergents, temperature, and dissolved solids may be present in wastewaters, but are not expected to be significant. No toxic or hazardous compounds are known to be present in flat glass industry wastewaters.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: TSS, oil, phosphorus and pH are the regulated pollutants for the flat glass industry, float glass production, (see 40 CFR Part 426, Subpart E) and were therefore selected for inclusion in the emissions inventory. EPA's ECHO tool was used to identify facilities that fall within this industry. Recent DMR data and permit limits were compiled for several facilities, selected at random. Effluent exchange values were selected based on reasoning provided in the modeling constants field. Excluded pollutants are discussed in the data completeness field.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Estimates of effluent pollutant concentrations were made based on judgement described in the Modeling Constants metadata field.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The scope of this treatment process includes process emissions from the release of treated effluent to surfacewater. Operation of unit processes necessary to produce treated effluent is covered in other linked processes. Uncertainty ranges are provided for phosphorus, TDS, and TSS. The low and high range is defined based on a limited review of facility DMR data and permit requirements. For TSS a range of 0-20 mg/L appears reasonable based on reported DMR data, treatment technologies and permit requirements. EPA's ECHO tool was used to identify facilities that fall within this industry. Permit data was identified through state regulatory agency websites.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process reflects only the process emissions associated with effluent release. Use the corresponding wastewater treatment processes to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts in the flat glass industry. Consider creating a new process or editing the existing effluent process if site specific data is available. The process includes an emission of water to water, reflecting treated effluent release. If a corresponding upstream extraction of water is not included in the product system  water consumption results will incorrectly show as negative.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication: This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public to reflect the impact of flat glass industry wastewater treatment within their product systems. This process must be used in conjunction with the associated wastewater treatment and sludge management processes to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts. The inventory should be sufficient to model TRACI 2.1 impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: This unit process was prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) on behalf of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory as part of their Federal LCA Commons curation activities.
